name: Strata
one_liner: Keyboard-first Linux file manager: Miller columns, Ctrl+K search, RAW/PDF/video previews

text.why: Spatial Miller-column navigation sits alongside Icons and List views, and Ctrl+K recursive search covers Home and all mounted local drives even while the tree is still being indexed. Previews for images, camera RAW, PDF, audio and video are produced by helpers isolated in a Bubblewrap sandbox with no network; plain-text and source previews stay in process, capped at 1 MiB. The installer verifies the SHA-256 digest and GitHub Actions build provenance before installing the binary, and on Omarchy it can replace the Nautilus shortcuts and even act as the system file chooser (portal).
text.take: A file manager riding the Omarchy wave, with a clear security posture: sandboxed preview parsers and build-provenance checks before install.
build: Beyond the six bundled themes you can write custom themes, and it follows the Omarchy Quattro theme live; with strata --install-portal you can make Strata the Open/Save chooser for portal-aware applications (apps that do not use the XDG Desktop Portal are unchanged).

who.situation: a Nautilus replacement wired to Super+Shift+F
Ctrl+K search, Ctrl+L path entry, Space to preview

who.role: People working with photos, video and documents
who.situation: RAW/PDF/video previews and media properties (resolution, codecs)

start.text: # Dependencies for a manual install on Arch / Omarchy
sudo pacman -S --needed bubblewrap ffmpeg ffmpegthumbnailer fontconfig gstreamer gst-libav gst-plugins-base gst-plugins-good gtk4 gtksourceview5 gvfs poppler-glib

caveat: Licence: the repository LICENSE file and README say MIT, but the official homepage FAQ says GPL-3.0-or-later — which is correct: [확인 필요]. 64-bit Linux only (x86_64, aarch64); glibc 2.39+ and GTK 4.12+ required. Arch and Omarchy are the primary supported environments and Wayland the primary display stack. SMB and phone access need extra GVfs backends. The project started at the end of August 2026. Free, no paid tier.
